m-intro.supports: Discrete models, proof, and computer-science applications.

m-propositions.supports: Statements, truth values, predicates, and counterexamples.

m-implication.supports: Direct and contrapositive implication proofs; both directions of an equivalence.

m-cases.supports: Proof by cases, contradiction, and clear mathematical argument.

m-wop.supports: Least counterexamples, well ordering, and prime-factor existence.

m-connectives.supports: Negation, conjunction, inclusive/exclusive disjunction, implication, and truth tables.

m-equivalence.supports: Validity, equivalent formulas, Boolean laws, and justified rewrites.

m-quantifiers.supports: Predicate domains, quantification, order, and negation.

m-sequences.supports: Indexed sequences and recursive integer functions.

m-functions.supports: Functions, composition, partial/total conventions, arrow diagrams, and finite cardinality. This notebook uses total functions unless stated otherwise.

m-relations.supports: Relations as ordered pairs and arrow representations.

m-induction.supports: Base case, induction hypothesis, implication step, and invalid induction.

m-strong.supports: Strong induction, recursive splitting, and equivalence with ordinary induction.

m-divisibility.supports: Divisibility, greatest common divisors, primes, and factorization.

m-digraph.supports: Directed degrees, walks, and adjacency matrices.

m-composition.supports: Relational composition, reachability, and positive/reflexive walk closures.

m-orders.supports: DAG scheduling, partial orders, cover representations, and total orders.

m-classes.supports: Equivalence classes, partitions, and relational properties.

m-graph.supports: Simple graphs, adjacency, degree sums, and common graph families.

m-walks.supports: Paths, components, and Euler/Hamiltonian walks. Terminology conventions are stated in the lesson.

m-trees.supports: Trees, forests, spanning trees, and equivalent tree properties.

m-sums.supports: Finite geometric and power sums, telescoping, and bounds.

m-products.supports: Products, factorial estimates, and sums with two indices.

m-asymptotic.supports: Eventual growth bounds, little-o, theta, and common asymptotic pitfalls.

m-counting.supports: Sum/product/division rules, ordered choices, combinations, and repetition.

m-pigeonhole.supports: Pigeonhole arguments and finite mapping constraints.

m-pie.supports: Inclusion–exclusion, binomial identities, and counting in two ways.

m-recursive.supports: Unfolding, Hanoi, merge sort, and recurrence verification.

m-linear-rec.supports: Characteristic roots, repeated roots, and nonhomogeneous linear recurrences.

m-divide-rec.supports: Recursion levels, divide-and-conquer recurrences, and bounds.

p-sets.supports: Set definitions, power sets, Cartesian products, indexed families, and Venn reasoning.

p-logic.supports: Connectives, conditional forms, truth tables, and logical equivalence.

p-quantifiers.supports: Quantifiers, English translation, negation, and logical inference.

p-direct.supports: Definitions, parity, divisibility, direct proof, and cases.

p-contra.supports: Contraposition, congruence examples, and mathematical writing.

p-contradiction.supports: Contradiction proofs, irrationality, and combining proof techniques.

p-setproof.supports: Element proofs of membership, inclusion, and equality.

p-disproof.supports: Genuine counterexamples and refuting existential assertions.

p-relations.supports: Relation properties, equivalence classes, and partitions.

p-functions.supports: Total functions, injectivity, surjectivity, inverses, images, and preimages.

p-multisets.supports: Stars and bars, division/pigeonhole principles, and combinatorial proof.

i-vectors.supports: Vector coordinates, addition, scaling, and linear combinations.

i-subspaces.supports: Subspaces, column spaces, and null spaces.

i-basis.locator: §§2.7.1–2.7.3: basis and dimension definitions; column-space and null-space bases; Basis Theorem and proof
i-basis.supports: Bases and dimension; extracting or extending a basis; selecting original pivot columns and homogeneous solution vectors. The equal-size basis theorem is stated; the lesson supplies its own exchange argument.

i-coordinates.supports: Unique coordinates relative to a basis.

i-rank.supports: Rank, nullity, and the rank theorem.

i-reduction.supports: Row operations, pivots, and echelon forms.

i-parameters.supports: Free variables and parametric solution sets.

i-transform.supports: Linearity and recovering a matrix from basis images.

i-multiply.supports: Composition, matrix products, transpose, and algebraic laws.

i-diagonal.supports: Eigenbases, repeated action, and failures of diagonalization.

i-dot.supports: Dot product, norm, angles, and orthogonality.

i-projection.locator: §§6.3.1–6.3.2: Orthogonal decomposition; Closest vector and distance; line-projection recipe and proof; projection properties

i-orthonormal.locator: §§6.4.1–6.4.2: orthogonal independence, Projection Formula, normalization, and Gram–Schmidt theorem/proof including zero remainders
i-orthonormal.supports: Orthogonal and orthonormal bases, projection sums, and Gram–Schmidt with span preservation and redundant-vector removal. The source orthogonalizes before normalizing; the lesson normalizes each retained direction.

i-least.locator: §§6.5.1–6.5.2: normal-equation theorem, uniqueness criteria, and Best-fit line
i-least.supports: Normal equations, orthogonal residuals, unique fitted outputs, rank-dependent parameter uniqueness, and least-squares fitting of vertical discrepancies. The source orders slope before intercept; the lesson orders intercept before slope and defines residual as observations minus fitted output.

ml-intro.supports: Motivation for mathematical data models and linear algebra.

ml-affine.supports: Linear maps, kernel/image, change of basis, and affine spaces.

ml-svd.supports: Full and reduced SVD, rectangular dimensions, singular directions, and numerical cautions.

ml-models.locator: §8.1, printed pp. 251–258 (PDF pp. 257–264), especially §8.1.4: fitting training observations versus predicting unseen data
ml-models.supports: Models, data, and the limits of mathematical interpretation.

d-intro.supports: Scope and examples of discrete mathematics.

alg-search.locator: Lectures 13–14: BFS; DFS and topological sorting
alg-search.supports: Adjacency lists, breadth/depth-first traversals, complexity, and scheduling.

alg-cost.locator: Lecture 2: Models of Computation; Recitation 1: asymptotic complexity
alg-cost.supports: Cost models, input size, asymptotic analysis, and worst-case interpretation.

tex-supported.supports: Math commands, grouping, scripts, spacing, and matrix/aligned/cases environments. Foundations supports a curated subset; editor controls are app-specific.

tex-delimiters.locator: Auto-render extension: delimiters and ignored text
tex-delimiters.supports: Inline/display math delimiters; Foundations uses its own parser and deliberately supports single-dollar inline math.

js-every.supports: Finite-array predicate checks and empty-array behavior.

js-some.supports: Finite-array predicate checks and empty-array behavior.

js-floor.supports: Rounding direction and the distinction between integer truncation and floor/ceiling.

js-ceil.supports: Rounding direction and the distinction between integer truncation and floor/ceiling.

js-trunc.supports: Rounding direction and the distinction between integer truncation and floor/ceiling.

history-logic.supports: Historical distinction between term logic and Stoic propositional logic.

history-graph.locator: E53: archive summary and English translation

svd-approx.locator: Low-rank approximation, Solution, and Relation to SVD
svd-approx.supports: Frobenius-optimal truncated SVD and residual error from discarded singular values.

numerical-rank.supports: Singular-value thresholds and the distinction between exact and numerical rank.

numerical-ls.locator: Linear Least Squares (LLS) Problems: xGELS paragraph, rank-deficient driver paragraph, and Table 2.3
numerical-ls.supports: QR/SVD methods, full-rank and rank-deficient least-squares problems.

alg-asymptotic.locator: Recitation 1, pp. 1–4: asymptotic complexity and binary search
alg-asymptotic.supports: Upper, lower, and tight bounds; logarithmic growth and binary-search recurrences.

i-determinant-area.locator: §4.3.2: Determinants and volumes theorem, transpose observation, Area example, and Signed volumes remark
i-determinant-area.supports: Absolute determinant as parallelogram area and determinant sign as orientation in the plane. The source first uses rows, then explicitly extends the volume statement to columns; the lesson uses columns.

i-existence-uniqueness.locator: §§3.2.1–3.2.3: one-to-one and onto matrix-transformation theorems; square-matrix comparison
i-existence-uniqueness.supports: Independent columns give at most one input per output; full row rank reaches every output. These are separate conditions for rectangular matrices and coincide for square matrices.

strang-row-space.locator: §3.5, printed pp. 182, 184–185 (PDF pp. 2, 4–5): nonzero echelon rows; The Four Subspaces for A, items 1–2
strang-row-space.supports: Nonzero echelon rows form a row-space basis; reversible row operations preserve row span; row rank and column rank equal the pivot count. Row reduction need not preserve the column space.

numerical-solve.locator: Linear Equations: simple-driver description and paragraph immediately before Table 2.2
numerical-solve.supports: Linear-system drivers factor the coefficient matrix and solve without explicitly forming its inverse; explicit inversion is generally unnecessary for solving systems.

lapack-qr.locator: QR Factorization: reduced factorization A=Q1 R and full-column-rank least-squares application
lapack-qr.supports: Orthonormal columns and upper-triangular reconstruction coefficients in reduced QR, matrix dimensions, and triangular least-squares solving. The lesson names the rectangular factor Q; this source names it Q1. LAPACK implementation is not claimed to use classroom Gram–Schmidt.

fnc-normal-stability.locator: The normal equations — Conditioning and stability, equations (65)–(66)
fnc-normal-stability.supports: Sensitivity of least-squares coefficients to perturbations and possible numerical instability from forming normal equations: in the 2-norm, the condition number of A transpose A squares that of A.

review-witness.locator: Quantifiers and Equality, The Existential Quantifier
review-witness.supports: A witness is a domain value satisfying an existential condition. Supports original definition recall prompts and generated integer examples, not copied source exercises. Integer examples independently checked by substitution.

review-logic-statements.locator: §1.1, Definition 1.1.5 and Atomic and Molecular Statements
review-logic-statements.supports: Statements with definite truth values, including false or unchecked claims; contrast with questions, commands, and unassigned free variables. Supports original retrieval prompts and examples, not copied textbook exercises.

review-logic-basics.supports: Propositions, truth values, negation, conjunction, disjunction, exclusive OR, implication, and biconditional names and truth conditions. Original prompts follow this curriculum's notation and examples.

review-logic-conditionals.supports: Antecedent and consequent roles; the sole false implication case; converse, inverse, and contrapositive; refutation by a case meeting the antecedent and violating the consequent. Prompts preserve curriculum terminology, which does not introduce hypothesis as an antecedent synonym.

review-logic-conditional-language.supports: Necessary and sufficient conditions; direction of if and only if; biconditionals assert both implication directions. Supports original wording and notation variants, not copied examples.

review-logic-equivalence.supports: Complete truth tables, independent truth assignments, equivalence by matching all rows, contraposition, De Morgan's laws, and implication rewrites. Original compound formulas and counterassignments were independently checked over every truth assignment.

review-logic-negation.supports: Negation of implication as a true antecedent with a false consequent; De Morgan transformations; strict versus non-strict inequality negation. Original boundary examples were independently checked below, at, and above each boundary.

review-logic-classification.supports: Precise distinction among tautology, contradiction, and contingency according to all possible truth assignments. Original retrieval items distinguish all, some, and no true rows.

review-logic-arguments.supports: Arguments, premises, conclusions, and validity as true premises forcing a true conclusion. Validity is distinct from the actual truth of the premises. Supports original definition and distinction prompts.

review-logic-counterassignments.supports: An assignment with every premise true and conclusion false refutes validity. Original counterassignment construction variants and feedback were checked independently by truth-table evaluation; the examples are not copied from the source.

review-logic-models.locator: Propositional Theories, numbered slide 9 (PDF page 8); Horn Bounds, numbered slide 11 (PDF page 10)
review-logic-models.supports: In propositional logic a model is an actual truth assignment under which the formula or theory is true. Supports the model terminology distinction; MIT references separately support satisfiability and unsatisfiability.

review-predicate-meaning.supports: Predicate inputs and substitution into a truth-valued condition. Supports original definition and distinction prompts, not copied exercises.

review-quantifier-meaning.supports: Universal and existential terminology and truth conditions, explicit domains, finite-domain interpretations, and witness membership. Original numeric examples independently verified.

review-domain-order.supports: Domains, mixed-quantifier order, dependent versus fixed witnesses, validity and countermodels. Supports original interpretations and constructions; examples independently checked.

review-variable-scope.supports: Scope, free and bound occurrences, formulas with no free variables, and safe renaming without capture. The curriculum uses explicit parentheses rather than relying on scope conventions; it calls formulas with no free variables closed.

review-quantifier-negation.supports: Negation of universal, existential, nested, and conditional quantified statements while preserving domains and variable order. Original comparison-boundary variants independently checked.

review-quantifier-counterexamples.supports: Domain-valid counterexamples to universal and conditional claims; refuting existence requires excluding all candidates. Original boundary and numeric examples independently verified.

review-unique-existence.supports: Exactly-one quantification as existence plus at-most-one uniqueness, including the zero-solution distinction. Matches the curriculum's explicit separation of existence and uniqueness.

review-empty-domain.supports: Universal truth and existential falsity for an explicitly empty domain; nonempty-domain requirement for inferring existence from a universal claim. The source normally assumes nonempty domains but explains the empty-domain contrast; the curriculum permits emptiness only when stated.

review-quantifier-distribution.locator: §§8.2–8.3, universal conjunction and existential disjunction proofs
review-quantifier-distribution.supports: Universal conjunction and existential disjunction distribution. The original separate-witness countermodel was exhaustively checked over its two-element domain.

mml-transpose.supports: Transpose shape and the row/column exchange defining each transposed entry; original numerical examples are independently calculated.
